channel.title: Sample Sports Wire
channel.description: Offline sample feed bundled with Touchline Takes. Fictional stories for testing only.

item.title: Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 in tense London derby
item.description: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates on Saturday. Midfielder Tomas Reyes equalised before half-time and striker Leo Hartmann headed the winner in the 78th minute, lifting Arsenal to second in the Premier League.

item.title: Liverpool held to goalless draw by Everton in Merseyside derby
item.description: Liverpool were held to a 0-0 draw by Everton at Anfield. Everton goalkeeper Sam Okafor made seven saves as the visitors frustrated the Premier League leaders, who had 24 shots.

item.title: Manchester City thrash Wolves 4-0 to keep pressure on leaders
item.description: Manchester City thrashed Wolves 4-0 at the Etihad. Forward Kai Brandt scored twice and City have now won four Premier League games in a row, keeping the pressure on Liverpool.

item.title: Tottenham boss sacked after 3-0 defeat at Brentford
item.description: Tottenham have sacked head coach Marco Lindqvist after a 3-0 defeat at Brentford left the club 14th in the Premier League. Fans were furious after a sixth defeat in nine games, and the board said a change was needed.

item.title: Newcastle in talks to sign Dortmund winger Felix Amari
item.description: Newcastle are in talks with Borussia Dortmund over a January transfer for winger Felix Amari. The 23-year-old has scored six goals this season and Newcastle are weighing a fee of around 40 million euros.

item.title: Aston Villa captain ruled out for six weeks with hamstring injury
item.description: Aston Villa captain Dan Mercer has been ruled out for six weeks with a hamstring injury suffered against Fulham. Villa will be without their captain for the busy December schedule, a blow to their top-four hopes.

item.title: VAR controversy as Brighton denied late penalty against West Ham
item.description: Brighton were furious after VAR declined to award a late penalty in their 1-1 draw with West Ham. Manager Oscar Feld said the decision was a disgrace and the club has asked referees body PGMOL for an explanation.

item.title: Real Madrid stunned 2-0 by Sevilla in La Liga upset
item.description: Real Madrid suffered a shock 2-0 defeat away at Sevilla in La Liga. Sevilla striker Ivan Molero scored both goals as Real Madrid dropped to third, two points behind Barcelona.
